identity.name: Ammonium alginate
identity.chemical_class: Ammonium salt of alginic acid (alginate hydrocolloid polysaccharide)

function.mechanism: Increases viscosity and water binding, stabilizes dispersed phases, and forms gel-like matrices in food systems.

adi.basis: EFSA 2017 re-evaluation concluded there was no need for a numerical ADI for E400-E404 and no safety concern at refined exposure for reported uses.

efsa.key_finding: No numerical ADI needed for general reported uses; insufficient data for adequate safety assessment in infants/young children consuming specific FSMP categories (13.1.5.1/13.1.5.2).

fda.notes: Affirmed in Part 184 (GRAS) with specific category/maximum use limits (e.g., 0.4-0.5% in listed categories; 0.1% in all other categories for specified functions).

adi.basis: WHO JECFA database entry for ammonium alginate lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED.

notable_bans: EU suspended placing on market/import of jelly mini-cups containing specified gel-forming additives including E403 (Decision 2004/37/EC context cited in EFSA 2017 opinion).

concerns.summary: Gastrointestinal side effects have been reported at therapeutic-dose infant medicinal use levels (around 417-834 mg/kg bw/day as sodium alginate equivalents), and EFSA found data insufficient for specific infant FSMP categories.
EFSA noted potential hypersensitivity issues related to protein impurities and recommended minimizing protein limits in specifications.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA concluded no concern with respect to genotoxicity for alginic acid and its salts including E403.
EFSA considered alginic acid and its salts not of concern with respect to carcinogenicity in reviewed long-term studies.

populations: Infants and young children consuming special medical purpose foods
adi_exceedance.notes: A numerical ADI is not set (EFSA/JECFA non-numerical conclusion). Main risk-management caveat is vulnerable infant FSMP use rather than numeric ADI exceedance.

risk_assessment.rationale: Major regulators maintain approval/GRAS status and EFSA/JECFA assign non-numerical ADI outcomes, with no clear genotoxic/carcinogenic signal at food-use levels; however, infant FSMP-specific data gaps and high-dose GI effects justify not classifying as risk_free.
key_factors: EFSA 2017: no numerical ADI needed and no safety concern for reported uses
FDA: affirmed GRAS with specific use limits in 21 CFR 184.1133
No IARC listing found for ammonium alginate/CAS 9005-34-9
Caveat: inadequate data for certain infant FSMP categories
